mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPI YoY > 2% does not lead to tighter monetary policy within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% signals a tightening labor market, which leads to increased wage pressures and higher corporate costs, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE < 4% does not lead to increased wage pressures within 6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) over 3 months signals increased economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of instances following a sustained increase in HOUST, or HOUST increase does not correlate with increased economic activity over a 6-month period.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above 2% MoM signals increased economic output and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO MoM > 2% does not correlate with increased corporate earnings over a 1-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) by more than 0.25% in a month signals a loosening monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or FEDFUNDS decrease does not lead to loosening monetary policy within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in real personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals robust economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the joint increase in RSAFS and decrease in UNRATE does not correlate with robust economic growth over a 3-month period.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 in a month signals strong job growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase does not correlate with strong job growth over a 1-month period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) over 3 months signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances following a sustained increase in FEDFUNDS, or FEDFUNDS increase does not correlate with tightening monetary policy over a 6-month period.
